# .devcontainer/Dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    libaio1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \
    btop \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Oracle Instant Client (basiclite) — python-oracledb THICK mode needs it.
# TIA QA (tiafsqa) is older than 12.1 and resets THIN connections (DPY-4011),
# so the live pull runs thick, exactly like DBeaver's OCI driver. The pipeline
# reads $ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB (conf/base/parameters.yml -> oracle.lib_dir); we set
# it below and register the lib dir with ldconfig so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is optional.
# libaio1 (installed above) is the only shared-lib dependency.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linuxx64.zip" ;; \
      arm64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linux-arm64.zip" ;; \
      *) url="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$url" ]; then \
      mkdir -p /opt/oracle; \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$tmp/ic.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \
      echo /opt/oracle/instantclient > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/oracle-instantclient.conf; \
      ldconfig; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no Oracle Instant Client build for arch=$arch; thick mode unavailable"; \
    fi
ENV ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB=/opt/oracle/instantclient

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — provides the `omc` command used to wire
# the HUD statusline / hooks / agents (via `omc setup`) and the HUD npm fallback.
# Matches the host machine's setup; omc self-updates so we track latest.
RUN npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest

# AWS session tooling — so the Azure-federated STS login can be refreshed FROM
# INSIDE this container, not only on the WSL host. The artifact root is S3
# (PSDP_DATA_ROOT) with 12h tokens, so "my session died mid-session" is routine;
# previously it meant dropping out to a host terminal. See scripts/azlogin.
#
#   aws CLI v2       : `aws sts get-caller-identity` is how scripts/az_login.sh
#                      authoritatively verifies a login (the tool's exit code
#                      lies), plus general S3 work against the artifact root.
#   chromium (apt)   : NOT used as the browser — puppeteer ships its own
#                      version-matched build. This is here for its shared-library
#                      dependencies (libnss3/libgbm1/libasound2/…), which that
#                      bundled Chromium needs; the binary is a fallback you can
#                      select with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.
#   aws-azure-login  : the SAML login itself. Pinned — 3.6.x is what the login
#                      flow in scripts/az_login.sh is written against.
#
# The npm install is guarded: puppeteer's postinstall is what fetches that
# matched Chromium, and npm 11 already warns that the script is "not yet covered
# by allowScripts". It still runs today, but the day it stops, .local-chromium is
# silently empty and the login breaks at runtime, in the user's terminal, weeks
# later. --foreground-scripts puts the download in the build log and the `test -d`
# turns that failure into a failed image build instead.
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) a="x86_64" ;; \
      arm64) a="aarch64" ;; \
      *) a="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$a" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-${a}.zip" -o "$tmp/awscliv2.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/awscliv2.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      "$tmp/aws/install" --update; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no AWS CLI v2 build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi; \
    npm install -g --foreground-scripts aws-azure-login@3.6.4; \
    test -d /usr/lib/node_modules/aws-azure-login/node_modules/puppeteer/.local-chromium

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data-pipeline CLI tooling — chosen for THIS project's artifacts:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the pipeline's parquet/csv/xlsx without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select status,count(*) from
#            'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1"
#   yq     : query/validate the owned SQL + taxonomy YAML (source_queries /
#            error_taxonomy / scope) from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no duckdb/yq build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi

# eza / delta / dust (not in Debian stable) + starship prompt.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) t="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      arm64) t="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      *) t="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$t" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/latest/download/eza_${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/0.18.2/delta-0.18.2-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bootandy/dust/releases/download/v1.1.1/dust-v1.1.1-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name eza   | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/eza; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name delta | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/delta; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name dust  | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/dust; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    fi; \
    curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y

RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs once on container create/rebuild. Sequential + idempotent so the whole
# environment (uv, deps, Claude Code, oh-my-claudecode, HUD, hooks, shell) is
# set up automatically with no manual steps. Safe to re-run.
set -uo pipefail
log() { echo "[post-create] $*"; }
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Canonical OMC marketplace URL — matches the host machine's settings.json.
OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL="https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"

# 1. uv (for the vscode user; the Dockerfile installs it for root)
if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing uv"
  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi

# 2. Project dependencies — a project-local .venv the scripts/launch.json expect
#    (.venv/bin/python). Install the package editable with the dev + notebooks
#    extras, plus oracledb (thick-mode driver for the live TIA/Oracle pull; it
#    is imported by src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/.../oracle_source.py but not pinned in the
#    project metadata, so we add it explicitly). This mirrors the working host
#    venv (kedro-viz, plotly, ipykernel, pytest, s3fs, oracledb all present).
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then
  log "creating .venv (python 3.12)"
  uv venv --python 3.12 || log "WARN: uv venv failed"
  log "installing project + dev,notebooks extras + oracledb"
  uv pip install -e ".[dev,notebooks]" oracledb || log "WARN: dependency install failed"
fi

# 2b. VisiData — interactive terminal explorer for the pipeline's data artifacts
#     (parquet findings/intermediates, xlsx golden masters, csv drilldowns).
#     Installed isolated via `uv tool` so it never touches the project venv.
if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing visidata (uv tool)"
  uv tool install 'visidata[parquet]' 2>/dev/null \
    || uv tool install visidata \
    || log "WARN: visidata install failed (non-fatal)"
fi

# 2d. nbstripout git filter — .gitattributes marks *.ipynb/*.zpln with
#     filter=nbstripout, but the clean/smudge commands live in the per-clone
#     .git/config (not the repo). Point them at THIS container's .venv python so
#     notebook outputs are stripped on commit. `--install` is idempotent and
#     rewrites any stale absolute path from a previous machine. nbstripout ships
#     in the notebooks extra installed above.
if [ -f pyproject.toml ] && [ -x .venv/bin/python ] && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring nbstripout git filter (.venv)"
  .venv/bin/python -m nbstripout --install --attributes .gitattributes \
    || log "WARN: nbstripout filter install failed"
fi

# 3. Claude Code (install or update to latest)
log "installing/updating Claude Code (latest)"
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: claude install failed"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 4. oh-my-claudecode plugin (latest) — provides the /oh-my-claudecode:* skills
if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "setting up oh-my-claudecode plugin"
  claude plugin marketplace add "$OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL" || log "WARN: omc marketplace add failed"
  claude plugin marketplace update omc || true
  claude plugin install oh-my-claudecode@omc || log "WARN: omc plugin install failed"
else
  log "WARN: claude not on PATH; skipping oh-my-claudecode plugin"
fi

# 5. omc CLI + `omc setup` — installs the HUD statusline wrapper, hooks, agents
#    and skills into ~/.claude (the piece that gives the host its HUD niceties).
#    The CLI is baked into the image (Dockerfile); install per-user if missing.
if ! command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing omc CLI (oh-my-claude-sisyphus)"
  npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest 2>/dev/null \
    || sudo npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    || log "WARN: omc CLI install failed"
fi
if command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "running omc setup (HUD + hooks + agents + skills)"
  omc setup --quiet || log "WARN: omc setup failed"
else
  log "WARN: omc CLI unavailable; HUD/hooks may be incomplete"
fi

# 6. pre-commit git hooks (only if the repo defines them)
if [ -f .pre-commit-config.yaml ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing pre-commit hooks"
  uv run pre-commit install || log "WARN: pre-commit install failed"
fi

# 6a. Azure CLI + azure-devops extension — the repo lives on
#     dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice, so `az repos pr` / `az pipelines` /
#     `az boards` is the terminal path to PRs, builds and work items
#     (gh only speaks GitHub). Idempotent: skipped when already installed.
if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing Azure CLI"
  curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash || log "WARN: azure-cli install failed"
fi
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! az extension show --name azure-devops >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "adding azure-devops extension"
  az extension add --name azure-devops || log "WARN: azure-devops extension install failed"
fi

# 6b. Azure DevOps CLI defaults — org/project set once so no command needs
#     flags. Auth: export AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (e.g. via the repo's .env) for
#     non-interactive use, or `az login` / `az devops login` interactively.
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring az devops org/project defaults"
  az devops configure --defaults \
    organization=https://dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice \
    "project=Data Science and Advanced Analytics" \
    || log "WARN: az devops configure failed"
else
  log "WARN: az not on PATH (azure-cli feature missing?); skipping ADO defaults"
fi

# 6c. Azure DevOps aliases — oh-my-zsh sources every $ZSH_CUSTOM/*.zsh file.
ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR="${ZSH_CUSTOM:-$HOME/.oh-my-zsh/custom}"
if [ -d "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR" ]; then
  log "writing azure-devops aliases ($ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh)"
  cat > "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh" <<'EOF'
# Azure DevOps shortcuts (org/project defaults set by post-create.sh)
alias adopr='az repos pr create --draft --open'      # current branch -> draft PR
alias adoprs='az repos pr list --status active -o table'
alias adoruns='az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table'
EOF
fi

# 7. Handy command cheatsheet (shown by ~/.zshrc on interactive login)
mkdir -p ~/.config/dev-bootstrap
cat > ~/.config/dev-bootstrap/commands.txt <<'EOF'
source .venv/bin/activate            # activate the project venv
scripts/run.sh offline               # rebuild ledgers + deliverables (no DB)
scripts/run.sh full                  # live TIA + Django pull -> ledgers -> deliverables
kedro run --pipeline figures         # just redraw the two infographics
kedro viz                            # interactive pipeline graph (port 4141, auto-forwarded)
scripts/run_notebooks.sh             # rerun the audit notebooks (notebook<->pipeline smoke test)
pytest -q                            # reconciliation + source-contract gates
python -m policy_schedule_data_pipeline.core.data_paths          # which window/pull is current
duckdb -c "select outcome, count(*) n from 'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1 order by n desc"
vd data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet                   # browse the ledger (VisiData)
yq '.tia_log' src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/reference/source_queries.yaml   # the SQL, as owned data
az repos pr create --draft --open    # current branch -> draft PR (alias: adopr)
az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table  # recent pipeline runs (alias: adoruns)
# A live pull needs TIA_PASSWORD + PG_DJANGO_PROD_PASSWORD (both in .env).
# ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB is preset to the Instant Client baked into this image.
# NOTE: a full pull re-reads the MUTABLE TIA.POLICY, which re-dates the
# landed / phantom / MTA numbers on every artifact. Offline runs never do.
EOF

# 8. Mirror the host's Claude niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json.
#    Merged via jq so existing keys survive. This wires:
#      - HUD statusline        - agent teams (needs tmux, in image)
#      - vim editor mode       - tmux teammates + fullscreen TUI
#      - verbose output        - the OMC plugin + marketplace
#    plus bypassPermissions, which is container-specific (sandboxed vscode user).
mkdir -p ~/.claude
SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
[ -s "$SETTINGS" ] || echo '{}' > "$SETTINGS"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  jq \
    '.permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"
     | .env["CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS"] = "1"
     | .statusLine = {"type": "command", "command": "node ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hud/omc-hud.mjs"}
     | .enabledPlugins["oh-my-claudecode@omc"] = true
     | .extraKnownMarketplaces.omc.source = {"source": "git", "url": "https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"}
     | .editorMode = "vim"
     | .verbose = true
     | .teammateMode = "tmux"
     | .tui = "fullscreen"' \
    "$SETTINGS" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$SETTINGS"
  log "merged HUD + OMC niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json"
else
  log "WARN: jq missing; could not write ~/.claude/settings.json"
fi

# 9. Shell: link the shared dotfiles (zshrc / starship / tmux) from ~/env.
#    ~/env is bind-mounted read-only from the host (see devcontainer.json), so a
#    single source of truth drives the host and every container.
ENV_DIR="$HOME/env"
if [ -x "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" ]; then
  log "linking dotfiles from $ENV_DIR"
  "$ENV_DIR/install.sh" --link || log "WARN: dotfile link failed"
else
  log "NOTE: ~/env not mounted; using default shell config"
fi

# 10. zsh-history-substring-search (not packaged on Debian)
HSS="$HOME/.zsh/plugins/zsh-history-substring-search"
[ -d "$HSS" ] || git clone --depth=1 \
  https://github.com/zsh-users/zsh-history-substring-search "$HSS" || true

log "done"

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \

    graphviz \

# so the live pull runs thick, exactly like DBeaver's OCI driver. The pipeline
# reads $ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB (conf/base/parameters.yml -> oracle.lib_dir); we set
# it below and register the lib dir with ldconfig so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is optional.
# libaio1 (installed above) is the only shared-lib dependency.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linuxx64.zip" ;; \
      arm64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linux-arm64.zip" ;; \
      *) url="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$url" ]; then \
      mkdir -p /opt/oracle; \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$tmp/ic.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \
      echo /opt/oracle/instantclient > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/oracle-instantclient.conf; \
      ldconfig; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no Oracle Instant Client build for arch=$arch; thick mode unavailable"; \
    fi
ENV ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB=/opt/oracle/instantclient

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — provides the `omc` command used to wire
# the HUD statusline / hooks / agents (via `omc setup`) and the HUD npm fallback.
# Matches the host machine's setup; omc self-updates so we track latest.
RUN npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest

# AWS session tooling — so the Azure-federated STS login can be refreshed FROM
# INSIDE this container, not only on the WSL host. The artifact root is S3
# (PSDP_DATA_ROOT) with 12h tokens, so "my session died mid-session" is routine;
# previously it meant dropping out to a host terminal. See scripts/azlogin.
#
#   aws CLI v2       : `aws sts get-caller-identity` is how scripts/az_login.sh
#                      authoritatively verifies a login (the tool's exit code
#                      lies), plus general S3 work against the artifact root.
#   chromium (apt)   : NOT used as the browser — puppeteer ships its own
#                      version-matched build. This is here for its shared-library
#                      dependencies (libnss3/libgbm1/libasound2/…), which that
#                      bundled Chromium needs; the binary is a fallback you can
#                      select with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.
#   aws-azure-login  : the SAML login itself. Pinned — 3.6.x is what the login
#                      flow in scripts/az_login.sh is written against.
#
# The npm install is guarded: puppeteer's postinstall is what fetches that
# matched Chromium, and npm 11 already warns that the script is "not yet covered
# by allowScripts". It still runs today, but the day it stops, .local-chromium is
# silently empty and the login breaks at runtime, in the user's terminal, weeks
# later. --foreground-scripts puts the download in the build log and the `test -d`
# turns that failure into a failed image build instead.
RUN set -eux; \
    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) a="x86_64" ;; \
      arm64) a="aarch64" ;; \
      *) a="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$a" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-${a}.zip" -o "$tmp/awscliv2.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/awscliv2.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      "$tmp/aws/install" --update; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no AWS CLI v2 build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi; \
    npm install -g --foreground-scripts aws-azure-login@3.6.4; \
    test -d /usr/lib/node_modules/aws-azure-login/node_modules/puppeteer/.local-chromium

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data-pipeline CLI tooling — chosen for THIS project's artifacts:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the pipeline's parquet/csv/xlsx without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select status,count(*) from
#            'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1"
#   yq     : query/validate the owned SQL + taxonomy YAML (source_queries /
#            error_taxonomy / scope) from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install/update Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode: CLIs, OMC plugin, HUD
# statusline, hooks, and ~/.claude/settings.json niceties.
#
# Called by .devcontainer/post-create.sh on container create, and safe to
# re-run manually any time something looks broken:
#
#   scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh
#
# Both CLIs are also baked into the devcontainer IMAGE (see
# .devcontainer/Dockerfile), so `claude` exists even if this script never ran —
# this script's job is updating to latest and wiring the plugin/HUD/settings.
set -uo pipefail
log() { echo "[setup-claude-omc] $*"; }
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Canonical OMC marketplace URL — matches the host machine's settings.json.
OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL="https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"

npm_g() {  # global npm install with sudo fallback (image prefix is root-owned)
  npm install -g "$@" 2>/dev/null || sudo npm install -g "$@"
}

# 1. Claude Code + omc CLI: update to latest (npm, matching the image install);
#    if npm is somehow unavailable, fall back to the native installer, which
#    puts a per-user binary in ~/.local/bin.
if command -v npm >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing/updating Claude Code + omc CLI (npm -g)"
  npm_g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    || log "WARN: npm -g install failed"
fi
if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "claude not on PATH; trying native installer"
  curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: native install failed"
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi
if ! command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "ERROR: claude still not on PATH — aborting (omc setup needs it)"
  exit 1
fi
log "claude: $(claude --version 2>/dev/null | head -1)"

# 2. oh-my-claudecode plugin — provides the /oh-my-claudecode:* skills.
#    marketplace add fails harmlessly if it is already registered.
log "wiring oh-my-claudecode plugin"
claude plugin marketplace add "$OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL" 2>/dev/null || true
claude plugin marketplace update omc || true
claude plugin install oh-my-claudecode@omc || log "WARN: omc plugin install failed"

# 3. omc setup — installs the HUD statusline wrapper, hooks, agents and skills
#    into ~/.claude.
if command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "running omc setup (HUD + hooks + agents + skills)"
  omc setup --quiet || log "WARN: omc setup failed"
else
  log "WARN: omc CLI unavailable; HUD/hooks may be incomplete"
fi

# 4. Merge the host's Claude niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json (jq merge,
#    existing keys survive). bypassPermissions is container-specific (sandboxed
#    vscode user); DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER because the npm -g install is root-owned
#    — updates happen by re-running this script, not by claude self-updating.
mkdir -p ~/.claude
SETTINGS="$HOME/.claude/settings.json"
[ -s "$SETTINGS" ] || echo '{}' > "$SETTINGS"
if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  jq \
    '.permissions.defaultMode = "bypassPermissions"
     | .env["CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS"] = "1"
     | .env["DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER"] = "1"
     | .statusLine = {"type": "command", "command": "node ${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}/hud/omc-hud.mjs"}
     | .enabledPlugins["oh-my-claudecode@omc"] = true
     | .extraKnownMarketplaces.omc.source = {"source": "git", "url": "https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"}
     | .editorMode = "vim"
     | .verbose = true
     | .teammateMode = "tmux"
     | .tui = "fullscreen"' \
    "$SETTINGS" > "$tmp" && mv "$tmp" "$SETTINGS"
  log "merged HUD + OMC niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json"
else
  log "WARN: jq missing; could not write ~/.claude/settings.json"
fi

log "done — run scripts/devcontainer_doctor.sh to verify"

  || bad "claude missing" "scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Runs once on container create/rebuild. Sequential + idempotent so the whole
# environment (uv, deps, Claude Code, oh-my-claudecode, HUD, hooks, shell) is
# set up automatically with no manual steps. Safe to re-run.
set -uo pipefail
log() { echo "[post-create] $*"; }
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# Canonical OMC marketplace URL — matches the host machine's settings.json.
OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL="https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/oh-my-claudecode.git"

# 1. uv (for the vscode user; the Dockerfile installs it for root)
if ! command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing uv"
  curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
  export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
fi

# 2. Project dependencies — a project-local .venv the scripts/launch.json expect
#    (.venv/bin/python). Install the package editable with the dev + notebooks
#    extras, plus oracledb (thick-mode driver for the live TIA/Oracle pull; it
#    is imported by src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/.../oracle_source.py but not pinned in the
#    project metadata, so we add it explicitly). This mirrors the working host
#    venv (kedro-viz, plotly, ipykernel, pytest, s3fs, oracledb all present).
if [ -f pyproject.toml ]; then
  log "creating .venv (python 3.12)"
  uv venv --python 3.12 || log "WARN: uv venv failed"
  log "installing project + dev,notebooks extras + oracledb"
  uv pip install -e ".[dev,notebooks]" oracledb || log "WARN: dependency install failed"
fi

# 2b. VisiData — interactive terminal explorer for the pipeline's data artifacts
#     (parquet findings/intermediates, xlsx golden masters, csv drilldowns).
#     Installed isolated via `uv tool` so it never touches the project venv.
if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing visidata (uv tool)"
  uv tool install 'visidata[parquet]' 2>/dev/null \
    || uv tool install visidata \
    || log "WARN: visidata install failed (non-fatal)"
fi

# 2d. nbstripout git filter — .gitattributes marks *.ipynb/*.zpln with
#     filter=nbstripout, but the clean/smudge commands live in the per-clone
#     .git/config (not the repo). Point them at THIS container's .venv python so
#     notebook outputs are stripped on commit. `--install` is idempotent and
#     rewrites any stale absolute path from a previous machine. nbstripout ships
#     in the notebooks extra installed above.
if [ -f pyproject.toml ] && [ -x .venv/bin/python ] && git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring nbstripout git filter (.venv)"
  .venv/bin/python -m nbstripout --install --attributes .gitattributes \
    || log "WARN: nbstripout filter install failed"
fi

# 3. Claude Code (install or update to latest)
log "installing/updating Claude Code (latest)"
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash || log "WARN: claude install failed"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

# 4. oh-my-claudecode plugin (latest) — provides the /oh-my-claudecode:* skills
if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "setting up oh-my-claudecode plugin"
  claude plugin marketplace add "$OMC_MARKETPLACE_URL" || log "WARN: omc marketplace add failed"
  claude plugin marketplace update omc || true
  claude plugin install oh-my-claudecode@omc || log "WARN: omc plugin install failed"
else
  log "WARN: claude not on PATH; skipping oh-my-claudecode plugin"
fi

# 5. omc CLI + `omc setup` — installs the HUD statusline wrapper, hooks, agents
#    and skills into ~/.claude (the piece that gives the host its HUD niceties).
#    The CLI is baked into the image (Dockerfile); install per-user if missing.
if ! command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing omc CLI (oh-my-claude-sisyphus)"
  npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest 2>/dev/null \
    || sudo npm install -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    || log "WARN: omc CLI install failed"
fi
if command -v omc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "running omc setup (HUD + hooks + agents + skills)"
  omc setup --quiet || log "WARN: omc setup failed"
else
  log "WARN: omc CLI unavailable; HUD/hooks may be incomplete"
fi

# 6. pre-commit git hooks (only if the repo defines them)
if [ -f .pre-commit-config.yaml ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing pre-commit hooks"
  uv run pre-commit install || log "WARN: pre-commit install failed"
fi

# 6a. Azure CLI + azure-devops extension — the repo lives on
#     dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice, so `az repos pr` / `az pipelines` /
#     `az boards` is the terminal path to PRs, builds and work items
#     (gh only speaks GitHub). Idempotent: skipped when already installed.
if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "installing Azure CLI"
  curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash || log "WARN: azure-cli install failed"
fi
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! az extension show --name azure-devops >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "adding azure-devops extension"
  az extension add --name azure-devops || log "WARN: azure-devops extension install failed"
fi

# 6b. Azure DevOps CLI defaults — org/project set once so no command needs
#     flags. Auth: export AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT (e.g. via the repo's .env) for
#     non-interactive use, or `az login` / `az devops login` interactively.
if command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  log "configuring az devops org/project defaults"
  az devops configure --defaults \
    organization=https://dev.azure.com/OMIDataOffice \
    "project=Data Science and Advanced Analytics" \
    || log "WARN: az devops configure failed"
else
  log "WARN: az not on PATH (azure-cli feature missing?); skipping ADO defaults"
fi

# 6c. Azure DevOps aliases — oh-my-zsh sources every $ZSH_CUSTOM/*.zsh file.
ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR="${ZSH_CUSTOM:-$HOME/.oh-my-zsh/custom}"
if [ -d "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR" ]; then
  log "writing azure-devops aliases ($ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh)"
  cat > "$ZSH_CUSTOM_DIR/azure-devops.zsh" <<'EOF'
# Azure DevOps shortcuts (org/project defaults set by post-create.sh)
alias adopr='az repos pr create --draft --open'      # current branch -> draft PR
alias adoprs='az repos pr list --status active -o table'
alias adoruns='az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table'
EOF
fi

# 7. Handy command cheatsheet (shown by ~/.zshrc on interactive login)
mkdir -p ~/.config/dev-bootstrap
cat > ~/.config/dev-bootstrap/commands.txt <<'EOF'
source .venv/bin/activate            # activate the project venv
scripts/run.sh offline               # rebuild ledgers + deliverables (no DB)
scripts/run.sh full                  # live TIA + Django pull -> ledgers -> deliverables
kedro run --pipeline figures         # just redraw the two infographics
kedro viz                            # interactive pipeline graph (port 4141, auto-forwarded)
scripts/run_notebooks.sh             # rerun the audit notebooks (notebook<->pipeline smoke test)
pytest -q                            # reconciliation + source-contract gates
python -m policy_schedule_data_pipeline.core.data_paths          # which window/pull is current
duckdb -c "select outcome, count(*) n from 'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1 order by n desc"
vd data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet                   # browse the ledger (VisiData)
yq '.tia_log' src/policy_schedule_data_pipeline/reference/source_queries.yaml   # the SQL, as owned data
az repos pr create --draft --open    # current branch -> draft PR (alias: adopr)
az pipelines runs list --top 5 -o table  # recent pipeline runs (alias: adoruns)
# A live pull needs TIA_PASSWORD + PG_DJANGO_PROD_PASSWORD (both in .env).
# ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB is preset to the Instant Client baked into this image.
# NOTE: a full pull re-reads the MUTABLE TIA.POLICY, which re-dates the
# landed / phantom / MTA numbers on every artifact. Offline runs never do.
EOF

# 8. Mirror the host's Claude niceties into ~/.claude/settings.json.
#    Merged via jq so existing keys survive. This wires:
#      - HUD statusline        - agent teams (needs tmux, in image)

FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    libaio1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \
    btop \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Oracle Instant Client (basiclite) — python-oracledb THICK mode needs it.
# TIA QA (tiafsqa) is older than 12.1 and resets THIN connections (DPY-4011),
# so the live pull runs thick, exactly like DBeaver's OCI driver. The pipeline
# reads $ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB (conf/base/parameters.yml -> oracle.lib_dir); we set
# it below and register the lib dir with ldconfig so LD_LIBRARY_PATH is optional.
# libaio1 (installed above) is the only shared-lib dependency.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linuxx64.zip" ;; \
      arm64) url="https://download.oracle.com/otn_software/linux/instantclient/instantclient-basiclite-linux-arm64.zip" ;; \
      *) url="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$url" ]; then \
      mkdir -p /opt/oracle; \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$tmp/ic.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/ic.zip" -d /opt/oracle; \
      ln -sfn "$(find /opt/oracle -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'instantclient_*' | head -1)" /opt/oracle/instantclient; \
      echo /opt/oracle/instantclient > /etc/ld.so.conf.d/oracle-instantclient.conf; \
      ldconfig; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no Oracle Instant Client build for arch=$arch; thick mode unavailable"; \
    fi
ENV ORACLE_CLIENT_LIB=/opt/oracle/instantclient

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — baked into the IMAGE so
# `claude` and `omc` exist even if post-create fails or is skipped. post-create
# (via scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh) updates both to latest and wires the OMC
# plugin/HUD/hooks; the npm prefix is root-owned so the settings merge disables
# claude's self-updater (updates go through the setup script instead).
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    && command -v claude && command -v omc

# INSIDE this container, not only on the WSL host. The artifact root is S3
# (PSDP_DATA_ROOT) with 12h tokens, so "my session died mid-session" is routine;
# previously it meant dropping out to a host terminal. See scripts/azlogin.
#
#   aws CLI v2       : `aws sts get-caller-identity` is how scripts/az_login.sh
#                      authoritatively verifies a login (the tool's exit code
#                      lies), plus general S3 work against the artifact root.
#   chromium (apt)   : NOT used as the browser — puppeteer ships its own
#                      version-matched build. This is here for its shared-library
#                      dependencies (libnss3/libgbm1/libasound2/…), which that
#                      bundled Chromium needs; the binary is a fallback you can
#                      select with PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH=/usr/bin/chromium.
#   aws-azure-login  : the SAML login itself. Pinned — 3.6.x is what the login
#                      flow in scripts/az_login.sh is written against.

# matched Chromium, and npm 11 already warns that the script is "not yet covered

# turns that failure into a failed image build instead.

    apt-get update; \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends chromium; \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) a="x86_64" ;; \
      arm64) a="aarch64" ;; \
      *) a="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$a" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://awscli.amazonaws.com/awscli-exe-linux-${a}.zip" -o "$tmp/awscliv2.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/awscliv2.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      "$tmp/aws/install" --update; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no AWS CLI v2 build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi; \
    npm install -g --foreground-scripts aws-azure-login@3.6.4; \
    test -d /usr/lib/node_modules/aws-azure-login/node_modules/puppeteer/.local-chromium

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data-pipeline CLI tooling — chosen for THIS project's artifacts:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the pipeline's parquet/csv/xlsx without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select status,count(*) from
#            'data/02_intermediate/*/batch_ledger.parquet' group by 1"
#   yq     : query/validate the owned SQL + taxonomy YAML (source_queries /
#            error_taxonomy / scope) from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no duckdb/yq build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi

# eza / delta / dust (not in Debian stable) + starship prompt.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) t="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      arm64) t="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      *) t="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$t" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/latest/download/eza_${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/0.18.2/delta-0.18.2-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bootandy/dust/releases/download/v1.1.1/dust-v1.1.1-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name eza   | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/eza; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name delta | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/delta; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name dust  | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/dust; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    fi; \
    curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y

RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip

# .devcontainer/Dockerfile
FROM mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/python:3.12-bookworm

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    git-lfs \
    jq \
    unzip \
    zip \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    sqlite3 \
    libgomp1 \
    graphviz \
    zsh \
    tmux \
    neovim \
    btop \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Node.js LTS (system-wide) — required for npx-based MCP servers, Claude Code
# plugins, and the oh-my-claudecode (OMC) HUD.
RUN curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - \
    && apt-get install -y nodejs \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Claude Code + oh-my-claudecode CLI (system-wide) — baked into the IMAGE so
# `claude` and `omc` exist even if post-create fails or is skipped. post-create
# (via scripts/setup_claude_omc.sh) updates both to latest and wires the OMC
# plugin/HUD/hooks; the npm prefix is root-owned so the settings merge disables
# claude's self-updater (updates go through the setup script instead).
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@latest oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest \
    && command -v claude && command -v omc

RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
ENV PATH="/root/.local/bin:/home/vscode/.local/bin:${PATH}"

# Modern CLI niceties (shared with ~/env). apt-provided:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    fzf bat fd-find ripgrep zoxide \
    zsh-autosuggestions zsh-syntax-highlighting \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Data CLI tooling:
#   duckdb : SQL straight over the corpus/artifacts without Python —
#            e.g. duckdb -c "select count(*) from 'data/sample/documents.jsonl'"
#   yq     : query/validate the YAML configs (configs/*.yaml, conf/base/*)
#            from the shell, jq-style.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) duck="amd64"; yqa="amd64" ;; \
      arm64) duck="arm64"; yqa="arm64" ;; \
      *) duck=""; yqa="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$duck" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/releases/latest/download/duckdb_cli-linux-${duck}.zip" -o "$tmp/duckdb.zip"; \
      unzip -q "$tmp/duckdb.zip" -d "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$tmp/duckdb" /usr/local/bin/duckdb; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_${yqa}" -o /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    else \
      echo "WARN: no duckdb/yq build for arch=$arch"; \
    fi

# eza / delta / dust (not in Debian stable) + starship prompt.
RUN set -eux; \
    arch="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"; \
    case "$arch" in \
      amd64) t="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      arm64) t="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;; \
      *) t="" ;; \
    esac; \
    if [ -n "$t" ]; then \
      tmp="$(mktemp -d)"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/eza-community/eza/releases/latest/download/eza_${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/dandavison/delta/releases/download/0.18.2/delta-0.18.2-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/bootandy/dust/releases/download/v1.1.1/dust-v1.1.1-${t}.tar.gz" | tar -xz -C "$tmp"; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name eza   | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/eza; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name delta | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/delta; \
      install -m755 "$(find "$tmp" -type f -name dust  | head -1)" /usr/local/bin/dust; \
      rm -rf "$tmp"; \
    fi; \
    curl -sS https://starship.rs/install.sh | sh -s -- -y

RUN python -m pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip
